name: Mirror Polydactyly-Vertebral Segmentation-Limbs Defects Syndrome
aliases: Mirror-Image Polydactyly with Vertebral Segmentation Anomalies
Mirror Polydactyly with Limb and Vertebral Defects

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Mirror Polydactyly-Vertebral Segmentation-Limbs Defects Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of mirror-image polydactyly affecting hands and/or feet
Radiologically confirmed vertebral segmentation defects including hemivertebrae or block vertebrae
Additional limb defects such as syndactyly, limb shortening, or hypoplasia
Positive family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance
Absence of intellectual disability or neurological impairment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: mirror polydactyly, vertebral segmentation anomalies, and limb malformations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic imaging; genetic testing may assist but is not definitive.

imaging: X-ray demonstrating vertebral segmentation anomalies (hemivertebrae, block vertebrae)
Radiographs showing mirror-image polydactyly and limb malformations
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Genetic testing may exclude other polydactyly syndromes
other: Clinical examination revealing symmetrical mirror-image polydactyly
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant transmission in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of syndactyly with intellectual disability in some cases
Central clefts of hands and feet rather than mirror polydactyly
Variable limb defects without vertebral anomalies

redFlags: Severe spinal deformities causing respiratory compromise
Presence of cardiac malformations requiring intervention
references: Orphanet: Mirror Polydactyly-Vertebral Segmentation-Limbs Defects Syndrome (ORPHA:3004)
